title: Check every tier actually fits
goal: Catch tiers that don't truly differ, are mis-levelled, or don't fit your class.

blocks.title: Differentiated in name isn't differentiated in fact
blocks.body:
AI will happily label three sections 'support', 'core' and 'stretch' — and sometimes that's all the difference is: the labels.

Before you print, check three things. Do the tiers genuinely differ in demand, not just in length? Is each one pitched at the right level? And do the examples fit your class — Indian names, ₹, familiar contexts?

blocks.question: The 'stretch' tier is the exact same questions as 'core' — just ten of them instead of five. Your move?

options.text: Fine — more questions means it's harder
Catch it — that's more work, not deeper work; ask for a task that applies or explains the idea
Leave it; the AI labelled it 'stretch', so it must be

blocks.explanation: Caught it. 👏 More of the same isn't a stretch — your fast finishers will be bored, not challenged. Real stretch asks them to explain, apply, or extend. Spotting the difference is exactly the judgement no tool has.

blocks.question: The word problems are all about baseball scores and dollars at a mall. For your Class 6 in Pune, that's a problem of…

options.text: Nothing — a sum is a sum

blocks.explanation: Right — the maths isn't wrong, it just won't land. Ask for cricket scores, ₹, and familiar names so students spend their energy on the learning, not on decoding the context.

blocks.question: How ready do you feel to check that your tiers genuinely differ and fit your class?
